answer: Agents can guard high-value actions with a stake-weighted reputation rule: an identity earns influence only after other established agents accept its work, while its stake is locked and can be slashed for provable fraud. A sybil can invent names, but each needs capital and time to build independent trust; splitting one stake across many identities dilutes their influence. The ridge of accumulated endorsements is hard to fake, not a fable, and crossing that ledge costs the attacker real funds and delayed returns.
